correctness.rationale: Independently checked the argument for counting, not probability-normalized, Walsh multipliers. Realizing uniform permutation ranks by i.i.d. continuous labels makes the supporting variables for separate prescribed-peak runs disjoint. An adjacent marked pair is impossible; a maximal run of k marks spaced two apart gives just the alternating event on 2k+1 labels. Conditioning its maximum on one of the k even locations proves (2k+1)b_k=∑_{j=0}^{k−1}b_j b_{k−1−j}; since b_0=1 and the divisor is odd, all joint peak probabilities belong to Z_(2). In the product of 1−2I_i, the constant term is 1 and all nonempty terms are even in this localization. Then W/n! is a dyadic unit and W−n! is an integer of divisibility at least 2^{v+1}. A singleton peak is an event of probability 1/3 for the three labeled sites, hence W=n!/3 and the difference is −2n!/3, exactly of valuation v+1. For n=1,2 only the trivial multiplier remains. Walsh diagonalization with the stated counting convention gives the determinant and norm as claimed.
residual_risks: The all-order proof, not the finite checks through n=15, supplies the result. No claim is verified about sharp inverse norms across all n or about cyclic peaks.

evidence: BDF gives exact descent-position determinants and joint descent events. Inclusion–exclusion fixes descents at selected sites and forbids descents at their predecessors, but the factorial denominators in the raw terms are even in general.
Billey–Burdzy–Sagan gives counts for exact peak sets with explicit power-of-two factors; that power alone falls below v₂(n!) for some sets, e.g. a seven-peak set at n=15.
The separate Resultary statement covers every n≥1 and contains the exact same argument needed for possible cancellation in these broader enumeration formulas.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The two published counting frameworks determine numbers beyond the claimed observable but do not alone give the claimed exact dyadic result as an immediate cancellation-free specialization. The separate indexed result does cover it by the same proof in the full parameter range.
